meta.title: Abrus Krishna Finance UI/UX Design — Case Study | Teknoppy
meta.description: How Teknoppy designed the UI/UX for abruskrishna.com, giving a KML-registered Kerala lending company a visually distinct, trust-first interface across eight loan products.

paragraphs.text: Abrus Krishna Finance is a Kerala Money-Lenders Act (KML) registered lending institution based in Guruvayoor, offering gold loans, doorstep gold loans, and a range of micro business, personal, home, and consumer goods loans.

paragraphs.html: Note: this case study is scoped to UI/UX design work specifically — see the separate WordPress Development case study for this client for the full build.

items.title: No visual distinction between loan products
items.text: Without deliberate design, eight loan types risked visually blending together, making it hard for a borrower to quickly identify the right page for their need.

items.title: No visual prominence for compliance and trust signals
items.text: KML registration and regulatory information weren't given visual weight, despite being critical for a borrower deciding whether to trust a lender with gold or personal documents.

items.title: No visual guide through the borrower journey
items.text: The loan process wasn't presented as a clear visual flow, leaving first-time borrowers uncertain what to expect before applying.

paragraphs.text: Teknoppy's goal was to design a UI/UX that could help borrowers quickly tell eight distinct loan products apart, make regulatory trust visually prominent rather than buried in body text, and guide first-time borrowers through the loan process with confidence.

sections.h2: A comprehensive range of services offered by Teknoppy and their outcomes

items.title: Distinct visual treatment per loan category
items.text: Gold Loan, Business Loan, and Micro Finance product groups use a consistent but distinguishable page design, so a borrower can tell at a glance which page matches their need.

items.title: Trust and compliance made visually prominent
items.text: KML registration and compliance information are treated as first-class visual elements on their own dedicated page, not buried in body copy.

items.title: A visual four-step process
items.text: Contact/Visit → Document Verification → Approval → Disbursement is designed as a clear visual flow on the homepage, giving first-time borrowers a mental model before they apply.

items.title: A visual language suited to a regulated business
items.text: Typography, color, and layout choices reflect the seriousness of a regulated lending business rather than generic template styling.

paragraphs.text: Discovery, wireframing, and visual design decisions specific to this project — timeline and key design choices — should be pulled from the project intake and added here once confirmed.

sections.h2: Abrus Krishna Finance's Final Outcome After Teknoppy's Work

items.q: What was the main UI/UX challenge for Abrus Krishna Finance?
items.a: Designing an interface that lets borrowers quickly distinguish between eight loan products while making regulatory trust visually clear for a first-time visitor.

items.q: How does the design build trust for a lending business?
items.a: KML registration and compliance details are given dedicated visual prominence rather than being left as plain body text, and the four-step loan process is laid out visually so borrowers know what to expect.

items.q: Is this the same project as Abrus Krishna Finance's WordPress development case study?
items.a: No — this case study covers UI/UX design work specifically. The WordPress development case study for this client covers the full site build.

items.q: Did this UI/UX work affect Abrus Krishna Finance's existing rankings?
items.a: This design work was scoped separately from the site's core content and development work, so it doesn't compete with the WordPress development case study or the site's loan product pages for the same search terms.
